page_title: Predictive Analytics: The Power to Predict Who Will Click, Buy, Lie, or Die, Revised and Updated

sources.entry: Predictive Analytics: The Power to Predict Who Will Click, Buy, Lie, or Die by Eric Siegel

summary.name: Predictive Analytics: The Power to Predict Who Will Click, Buy, Lie, or Die
summary.one_liner: A revised and updated 2016 popular-science book by Eric Siegel that explains how predictive analytics (machine learning) works and how it affects everyday life.
use_cases: Learning how machine learning affects everyday life
Understanding predictive analytics before a technical career
Reading case studies of prediction in business and government
Getting an introduction to big data and prediction concepts
Exploring the power and perils of predicting human behavior
summary.what_it_does: ["Introduces predictive analytics (aka machine learning) for a general audience, explaining how computers learn from data to predict individuals' future behavior.", "Covers many case studies across industries such as banking, healthcare, marketing, crime fighting, and politics, including examples from Target, Netflix, and IBM Watson.", "Describes the underlying science in a non-technical way, intended as a foundation for future hands-on practitioners.", "Discusses the ethical perils of prediction, such as privacy and use of crime-predicting computers in sentencing and parole."]
notable: Written for lay readers and experts alike rather than as a hands-on how-to guide
Includes 182 examples from companies such as Airbnb, Google, Netflix, and Uber
Author is former Columbia University professor and founder of Predictive Analytics World
Revised and updated 2nd edition, 368 pages, published January 2016
caveats: Explicitly not a hands-on technical guide; does not teach coding or practical implementation
The page does not state a price; purchase is via Wiley's site
